name: Matgo (Korean Go-Stop)
description: Matgo is the quintessential two-player variant of 'Go-Stop', a popular Korean fishing game played with Hwatu ('Flower Cards'). Using a 48-card deck where each group of four represents a month/flower, players attempt to capture cards to form scoring combinations (Yaku). The name 'Matgo' distinguishes the 2-player competitive style from the 3-player 'Go-Stop'. It is arguably the most popular mobile and online game in South Korea.

Using a 48-card deck where each group of four represents a month/flower, players attempt to capture cards to form scoring combinations (Yaku). history.origins: Hwatu cards were introduced to Korea by Japan (derived from Hanafuda) in the late 19th century. Go-Stop and Matgo evolved as Korean-specific rule sets in the mid-20th century.
timeline: 1990s: Computerized versions of Matgo lead to a national gaming craze.
Present: A cultural icon, often played during holidays like Chuseok, and a dominant force in Korean mobile gaming.
history.cultural: Symbolizes social bonding and moderate gambling in Korean tradition.
history.evolution: Matgo perfected the 2-player dynamic by increasing the points required to win and adding special 2-player 'Shakes' and 'Bombs'.

setup.players: Matgo is played by exactly two players: one dealer (seon) and one opponent. Play proceeds counterclockwise from the dealer. The two-player variant uses a higher point target (typically seven) than three-player Go-Stop (typically three).
setup.deck: 48 cards: 12 months, 4 cards each. Themes: Pine (Jan), Plum (Feb), Cherry (Mar)... Paulownia (Dec).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 10 cards. 8 cards are placed face-up on the table.

rules.objective: Score 7 or more points to 'Go' (continue for more points) or 'Stop' (end and win).
rules.gameplay:
1. Match a card from your hand with a card on the table of the same month.
2. Flip the top card of the deck; if it matches a table card, take that pair too.
3. **The Kiss**: If you match your hand card AND the deck flip matches the same pair, it's a 'Kiss' (Sseok), and you take all three.
keyRules: Cards match by month (flower); capture matching cards to your area.
Each turn: flip top card of stock to table, then play one card from hand; resolve captures after each step.
Reach agreed target (usually 5 or 7 points) then declare Stop to win the hand or Go to continue for higher score at risk of opponent winning.
Scoring from captured combinations: brights (kwang), animals (yul), ribbons (tti), junk (pi); special events (bomb, shake) apply.

strategy.basic: Prioritize 'Junk' (Pi) cards that contain the 'Shakes' or 'Bombs'. In Matgo, Junk cards are often the easiest way to hit the 7-point threshold. Don't chase Brights if you are missing the easier 10-Junk point.
strategy.intermediate: The Paulownia (Dec) and Rain (Nov) months are powerful. Paulownia junk cards are doubled, and 'Rain' cards are essential for certain high-scoring Yaku. Block your opponent from completing 'Godori' (Birds) at all costs.
strategy.advanced: Multipliers: If you 'Go' three times, your score is tripled. Only 'Go' if you have a guaranteed path to more points and your opponent has fewer than 5 points. If they hit 7 before you win, they 'Stop' and take all your potential winnings.
tips: Shake: If you have 3 cards of the same month in hand, 'Shake' them to double your points if you win.
Bomb: If you have 3 cards in hand and the 4th is on the table, you can 'Bomb' it to take all and clear the space.
